statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases to 22% and returns below the block threshold after an observed 0.81% NQ retracement ended the session's shallow-pullback sequence.
recommendation: Tail is back inside the watch band, so the mapped policy state returns to WATCH from BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. The retracement that was absent one hour ago has now occurred: NQ gave back 252.50 points from its 31,282.25 high and the Nasdaq Composite slipped beneath its opening print, which is direct evidence that mean reversion is functioning. Tail is held at 22% rather than lower because a long end that reversed from 5.18% back to 5.25% is now the mechanism pushing equities off their highs, and that channel remains open into the weekly close. The evidence-based danger window is narrowed to 19:00Z-21:00Z, covering the Friday power hour, the cash close and the futures weekend settlement. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: A genuine 0.81% NQ retracement from 31,282.25 and a Composite slip under its opening print invalidate the shallow-pullback structure as the 10-year reverses to 5.25%
body: NQ futures trade 31,029.75 (+269.25, +0.88%) on a quote timed 15:20:06Z, inside a session range of 30,760.25-31,282.25 from a 30,771.25 open on about 360.8k contracts, with a 31,047.50/31,048.00 bid/ask. The decisive change since the previous assessment is that the retracement which was then absent has now happened, and it is broad. NQ extended once more to 31,282.25, above the 31,259.25 high flagged an hour ago, then gave back 252.50 points, or 0.81%, and now sits essentially at the session midpoint rather than within 0.10% of the extreme. The cash index confirms it: NDX is 30,795.31 (+293.74, +0.96%) at 15:29:44Z, 222.22 points or 0.72% beneath its 31,017.53 high and only 58.24 points above the 30,737.07 low. The Nasdaq Composite is 27,169.67 (+298.07, +1.11%) at 15:32:54Z, which is below its own 27,216.91 open, so the opening dip that was bought back through the open one hour ago has been fully reversed and the cash session's entire post-open advance has been retraced. Repeated extension after a failed retracement was the specific amplifier that justified the block band at 14:32Z, and it is now invalidated rather than merely weakened. The mechanism behind the reversal is the long end, and it is verified by independent reporting: Treasury yields fell after the employment report and then rebounded, pushing equities off their highs. The 10-year is 5.25% at 15:14:45Z against a 5.24% previous close and a 5.16-5.26% range, reported up 1.8 basis points to 5.252%, having traded as low as 5.18% immediately after the release. The 30-year is up 2.6 basis points to 5.629%. The 2-year is 4.816%, also above its prior close after an intraday low near 4.712%, so the dovish payroll reaction has been unwound at both ends of the curve. Leadership faded with the index: SMH is $631.16 (+2.16%) at 15:30:48Z against a $636.25 high and a $629.00 low, and NVDA is $234.60 (+1.62%) at 15:30:41Z, sitting at its $234.23 session low after an intraday record of $237.87, with market capitalisation about $5.665 trillion. VIX is 15.75 (-0.64, -3.90%) at 15:15:16Z in a 15.42-16.24 range, so implied volatility has firmed modestly off the session low without approaching a violent-repricing regime. November WTI is $90.55, down 2.50%, after trading as low as $88.11 against a $93.51 high, a 5.8% intraday swing that has bounced rather than extended. The macro backdrop is verified and unchanged: the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported September nonfarm payrolls up 29,000 against a consensus near 90,000, the unemployment rate rising to 4.2% from 4.1%, average hourly earnings up 0.1% month-on-month and 3.0% year-on-year, participation at 61.8%, government payrolls down 17,000 and manufacturing payrolls up 9,000. August Factory Orders printed 0.1%, in line. Implied October rate-hike odds sit near 16-20%, down from 64% a week earlier. Tail falls five points to 22% because the amplifier stack that drove it to 27% has been dismantled by observation: the extension sequence has stopped, a genuine 0.81% retracement has occurred, price no longer holds near its extreme, the opening-auction continuation has been reversed, and semiconductor leadership has retraced from its high. Under the governing calibration, event magnitude belongs in Stress while Tail reflects only the observed path, and the observed path is now two-way. Tail is held at 22% rather than pushed to the floor because the long-end reversal is a live mechanism rather than a resolved one: a sustained 10-year break above the 5.26% session high alongside a loss of the 30,760.25 NQ low would re-open a directional leg, and that channel stays available into a Friday weekly close. Stress holds at 79% on a realised NQ range that has widened to 522 points, about 1.70%, against a carried 5.25% long-end regime and a 5.8% oil swing; high Stress coexisting with a watch-band Tail is the intended reading of a difficult but mean-reverting session. Confidence holds at 89%: current NQ futures, cash NDX, Composite, SMH, NVDA, VIX, 2-year, 5-year, 10-year and 30-year yields and oil levels are all in hand alongside the primary BLS release and corroborating current reporting of the yield reversal, and the seven-day calendar was re-verified directly against the BLS release schedule, the Federal Reserve FOMC calendar and the trade-balance schedule. That re-verification corrected one carried calendar error: September CPI is scheduled for 14 October, not 7 October, so it falls outside this window and has been removed, while the 7 October FOMC minutes for the 15-16 September meeting are confirmed. Breadth data was not obtained this hour, which is the main reason Confidence is not higher. The shared Finviz context was not used; its payload carries a 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z collection time and a partial collection status, placing it far outside the 90-minute freshness contract, so it contributed no evidence here.

lookbackSummary: Across the 24 preceding published Claude hours Tail ran from 21% up to 27% and ended the window in the block band. The window opened at 21% in the 15:00Z hour on 1 October, printed 20% for thirteen consecutive hours through the U.S. afternoon and the Asian session, then stepped to 21% at 07:00Z, 23% at 08:00Z and 22% at 09:00Z as the European-morning advance gained directional efficiency. It returned to 20% at 10:00Z and 11:00Z once a genuine retracement formed, reached 24% at 12:00Z when the employment report took out the session high, crossed into the block band at 25% at 13:00Z on the gap-higher cash open and peaked at 27% at 14:00Z once the opening dip was bought back to a new high. Stress ranged from 74% to 79% and ended at 79%; Confidence held between 87% and 89%. Only the 08:00Z, 09:00Z, 12:00Z, 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots were published as trend-up, and the current hour returns to mixed.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail at 22% for the current 15:00Z hour and the 16:00Z confirmation hour, then eases to 21% across the 17:00Z and 18:00Z midday stretch as thinning liquidity is assumed to reduce directional efficiency. No slot is published in the block band, because the amplifier stack that supported it has been invalidated by an observed retracement and an absolute VIX near 15.8 is inconsistent with violent repricing. The escalation condition, a sustained 10-year break above the 5.26% session high together with a loss of the 30,760.25 NQ low, and its invalidation, a hold of that low with the front end steady near 4.816%, are named explicitly on the near hours instead. A three-point uplift to 24% covers 19:00Z and 20:00Z, the Friday power hour and the cash close, where weekly-close and market-on-close flow meets a record-area level and a long end that has already reversed once today; that pairing is the narrowed danger window. CME equity index futures settle for the weekend at 21:00Z, so the final fourteen slots carry a flat 20% watch floor rather than a projected curve: a closed market offers no path to deny, and mapping an unresolved off-the-highs record-area weekly close into the lowest band would misrepresent it as benign. Confidence decays from 89% to 72% across that closed stretch while the Tail and Stress floors hold, because ageing evidence degrades certainty about the state rather than the state itself. The first live checkpoint is Monday's 14:00Z ISM Services PMI, with Wednesday's 18:00Z FOMC minutes the most credible delayed-second-leg mechanism for the long end; September CPI was verified for 14 October and therefore sits outside this window.

forecastDetail.comment: NQ has retraced 0.81% from the 31,282.25 session high to 31,029.75 and the Composite has slipped under its 27,216.91 open while the 10-year reversed to 5.25%; the observed retracement invalidates the failed-pullback amplifier that justified the block band one hour ago, so Tail maps back into the watch band.

A conditional confirmation hour: the 30,760.25 NQ session low and the 5.26% 10-year session high are the two levels that decide whether the orderly two-way read holds or a long-end-led downside leg opens. Nothing in this hour is observed yet, and no scheduled release falls inside it.

Midday liquidity is assumed to thin, which usually reduces directional efficiency and improves mean-reversion conditions; Tail eases one point on that assumption, conditional on the 10-year settling back under its 5.26% session high rather than extending.

With European cash markets shut, U.S.-only flow dominates and cross-border hedging pressure is assumed to fade. Tail is held at 21 on an expectation of persisting two-way structure; oil's bounce off the 88.11 low is the secondary item to watch.

The Friday power hour is the narrowest genuine risk window left in the session: weekly-close rebalancing flow meets a record-area index level and a long end that already reversed higher once today. The three-point uplift is conditional, and an orderly drift with VIX under 16 invalidates it.

Market-on-close imbalances print into the 20:00Z cash close and can produce a brief directional push that denies retracement in the final minutes. This hour also sets the weekly closing level carried into a closed weekend, so flow rather than news is the driver.
